original_title: After 'Crunching Hard' Through Their Final Months, Gears of War: E-Day Developers Are Reportedly Now Expecting Layoffs
summary_en: Months after a grueling crunch period, developers at The Coalition are reportedly bracing for potential layoffs. This follows significant restructuring within Xbox Game Studios and the recent dismissal of the game's story director.
ai_analysis: The challenging development cycle and subsequent layoff fears for Gears of War: E-Day highlight the precarious nature of AAA game development, even for high-profile franchises.

en.title: Gears of War: E-Day Developers Reportedly Fear Layoffs After Grueling Crunch
en.summary: Months after a grueling crunch period, developers at The Coalition are reportedly bracing for potential layoffs. This follows significant restructuring within Xbox Game Studios and the recent dismissal of the game's story director.
en.body:
The mood at The Coalition, the studio behind the highly anticipated **Gears of War: E-Day**, is reportedly one of anxiety rather than celebration. Despite nearing the completion of a project they've dedicated years to, sources suggest developers are bracing for potential layoffs. This follows a period of intense "crunching hard" in the final months of development, a common but often criticized practice in the gaming industry.

This unease stems from broader organizational shifts within Xbox Game Studios. The company has undergone multiple rounds of significant redundancies over the past year. While The Coalition's team had previously felt somewhat insulated due to their work on the flagship **Gears of War** franchise, these recent events have shattered that sense of security. "The mood is certainly 'let's not celebrate the game until we're three months post launch, just in case', which is very unusual," one source commented, illustrating the prevailing apprehension.

## The Shadow of Restructuring

Adding to the palpable tension, the **Gears of War: E-Day** team is reportedly concerned about being reorganized under Activision or facing further job cuts. These fears are not unfounded, given Xbox boss Asha Sharma's announcement of 3,200 job cuts across the company this year. More recently, major structural changes saw **Halo Studios** downsized and its franchise management shifted to Activision, which is also now overseeing veteran studio Rare. The uncertainty surrounding the future of Xbox's key franchises has left the **Gears of War** team "on edge."

The situation was further exacerbated by the "very demoralizing" layoff of **Gears of War: E-Day** story director Juan Vaca, who was reportedly let go just two weeks before the game's anticipated release. This event has amplified concerns that no one is truly safe, regardless of their role or the project's importance.

## What This Means for Fans

For fans eagerly awaiting the return to the origins of the iconic **Gears of War** franchise, this news casts a somber shadow. **Gears of War: E-Day**, developed with the help of Polish studio People Can Fly and built from the ground up in Unreal Engine 5, promises to be The Coalition's most ambitious title yet. The game is set to explore the pivotal moments of Emergence Day, showcasing a massive new city called Kalona. The potential for instability within the development team, however, raises questions about the long-term health of the franchise and the studio itself. Fans will undoubtedly be hoping for a smooth launch and continued support for this ambitious project.

## What's Next

**Gears of War: E-Day** is slated for a 2026 release. While an exact date has not been confirmed, industry speculation suggests a potential release in the latter half of 2026 to avoid direct competition with major titles like **Grand Theft Auto 6**. Fans will be watching closely for any further official announcements regarding the game and the status of The Coalition's development team.

content_raw: Gear of War: E-Day developers are reportedly in no mood to celebrate the game's imminent release, following months of overtime and fresh fears of further layoffs. That's according to a Eurogamer report that includes comments from various sources at The Coalition, Microsoft's dedicated Gears of War team that has been working on E-Day for the past five years. Microsoft has made numerous rounds of redundancies over that time, though staff at The Coalition say they previously felt somewhat insulated from the job losses due to their work on such a high-profile project. But as their time building Gears of War: E-Day has wound down — a period that has also reportedly seen them "crunching hard" — there are now serious concerns that layoffs may soon be on the horizon for them, too. "The mood is certainly 'let's not celebrate the game until we're three months post launch, just in case', which is very unusual," one source said. "We're just expecting the next wave [of layoffs], or being reorganized under Activision or something later this year," claimed another. Xbox boss Asha Sharma unveiled a plan to cut 3,200 jobs across the company this year back in July, when the first 1,600 redundancies were announced . Then, last month, a second batch of layoffs were confirmed alongside major structural changes that saw Halo Studios downsized and the franchise handed to Activision, which will also manage veteran British studio Rare . With such seismic changes for Xbox's flagship shooter franchise, suddenly nothing seemed as certain for its Gears of War team. Staff say they are now "on edge" for the hammer to drop, especially following the "very demoralizing" layoff of Gears of War: E-Day story director Juan Vaca, who was recently culled just two weeks before the game's release. "I can only imagine the heartbreak of spending all those years on a game to have the final stretch ripped away, completely out of your control," another source said, commented on Vaca's departure. "It's like you planned for a year on a meal for your family where everyone will be there and the day of, you get locked out of the building or something and can't join in." Microsoft declined to provide an official response to Eurogamer for its report, though it is understood that Microsoft has acknowledged staff have worked hard on getting E-Day out the door, and that this extra effort includes out-of-hours toil that will be repaid in additional holiday. Xbox is yet to detail when its final round of layoffs this year will take place, though even if The Coalition is told it's safe for now, some staff have suggested they still won't breathe a sight of relief. "It's hard to believe anything [Microsoft leadership] say anymore after discarding staff in this manner," one employee stated. Last week, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella described the Xbox layoffs as "streamlining" at the company that was "great to see."
